claims.text: The funding is for collaborative projects between the UK and Japan.
The funding covers projects across arts, culture, humanities, social issues, Japanese language, medicine, health, science, youth, education, and sport.
The aim of the funding is to encourage mutual understanding.
The aim of the funding is to encourage lasting collaboration.
The funding is described as 'seed funding'.
Awards will generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000.
Awards will only exceptionally exceed £6,000.
Applications are accepted for projects in all fields, including arts and culture, humanities and social issues, Japanese language, medicine and health, science, youth and education, and sport.
Projects should bring people in the UK and Japan together.
Projects should deepen mutual understanding.
Projects should encourage the exchange of ideas or expertise.
Projects should develop lasting collaboration between the UK and Japan.
Grant money can be used to support festivals, workshops, performances and other events that present aspects of Japan to the UK or the UK to Japan.
Grant money can be used to support exchanges between the two countries that enable participation and interaction.
Grant money can be used to support collaborative projects involving UK and Japanese participants that result in new and innovative outputs.
Grant money can be used to support the teaching and development of Japanese language and cultural studies in schools and higher education.
Grant money can be used to support academic research, visits and exchange, where these push forward the boundaries of knowledge and understanding or involve collaboration and co-production.
Projects that show genuine collaboration between the UK and Japan are of particular interest.
Projects that result in new outputs with clear benefits for people beyond the project itself are of particular interest.
Applicants must be able to demonstrate a realistic plan for delivering their project.
Applicants must be able to demonstrate a clear budget for their project.
Applicants must be able to demonstrate key dates and activities for their project.
Applicants must be able to demonstrate how support from the Foundation will make a meaningful difference to the project.
Most awards are considered on a case-by-case basis.
There is no formal limit on the amount that can be applied for unless applying for PhD research or travel costs.
For very small projects, grant funds may cover the whole project.
More normally, grant funds provide partial support, with applicants demonstrating secured or planned additional funding.
For travel and subsistence in Japan for PhD research from the UK office, up to £2,000 is awarded for trips up to 13 days.
For travel and subsistence in Japan for PhD research from the UK office, up to £2,500 is awarded for trips of 14 days or more.
These travel limits are consistently applied to projects involving travel for up to two people.
For three or more people traveling for PhD research from the UK office, a lower overall amount may be awarded to stay within the £1,500-£5,000 range.
The UK office may award up to £5,000 specifically for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more.
A compelling case is needed to justify an award of over £6,000.
The Japan office may award up to ¥300,000 for PhD students from Japan wishing to travel to the UK for fieldwork or research.
Grants are not made for consumables, salaries, or purchase of materials.
Grants are not made for capital projects such as the purchase, construction or maintenance of buildings.
Grants are not made for student fees.
Grants are not made for travel in connection with study for a qualification (excluding PhD students).
Grants are not made to support undergraduate or master’s students.
Grants are not made for retrospective activity.
Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds.
Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects.
The UK office may consider applications from individuals who can provide proof of organisational support.
Grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts.
Previous recipients are welcome to apply for new projects.
Applications for small grants can be submitted to both UK and Japan offices.
Projects originating in the UK should be submitted through the UK office.
Projects originating in Japan should be submitted through the Japan office.
The same project cannot be submitted to both offices.
Applications to the UK office must be made using a specific form.
Applications from PhD students to the UK office must include a letter of support from the PhD supervisor.
Applications and enquiries to the UK office must be sent by email to grants@gbsf.org.uk.
To apply to the Japan office, applicants should email tokyo@gbsf.org.uk for further details.
Applicants to the Japan office should not use the application form linked for UK applications.
Successful applicants must make a change request if anything substantial changes in their plans.
Successful applicants must acknowledge the Foundation's support in their own channels and use its logo in publicity material.
Successful applicants must contribute or collaborate on content for social media channels and/or the website and annual review.
Successful applicants must submit a brief post-project report shared with the Foundation within three months of completion.
The UK office holds three annual awards meetings with application deadlines on March 31, September 15, and December 15.
The Japan office holds two annual awards meetings with application deadlines on February 28 and September 30.
